statement: The range of the function $f$ is $-3 \le y \le 5$. The function $g$ is defined by $g(x) = -2f(x) + 1$. What is the range of $g$?

choices.misconception: I added the $1$ to each output of $f$ first and then multiplied by $-2$, but the $-2$ multiplies $f(x)$ before the $1$ is added.
I multiplied the endpoints $-3$ and $5$ by $-2$ and put them in order, but I forgot to add the $1$ afterward.
I multiplied by $2$ and added $1$ but ignored the negative sign, which flips the graph and swaps which end is the top.

hints: Apply the steps to the smallest and largest outputs of $f$: first multiply by $-2$, then add $1$.
Find $-2(-3) + 1$ and $-2(5) + 1$. Multiplying by a negative number reverses the order, so check which result is smaller.
The two values are $7$ and $-9$. Every output of $f$ between $-3$ and $5$ lands between them.

solutions.reliable: Every output $y$ of $f$ satisfies $-3 \le y \le 5$. Multiplying by $-2$ reverses the inequalities: $-10 \le -2y \le 6$. Adding $1$ gives $-9 \le -2y + 1 \le 7$. Since $f$ takes every value from $-3$ to $5$, $g$ takes every value from $-9$ to $7$, so the range of $g$ is $-9 \le y \le 7$.
solutions.elegant: The endpoints of the range move to $-2(-3) + 1 = 7$ and $-2(5) + 1 = -9$. The reflection swaps top and bottom, so the range is $-9 \le y \le 7$.
